description: FastAPI Python application (Reports, Documents, Integrations feature areas) with intentionally vulnerable request handling, some confined to a single file and some spanning the route/service boundary.

vulnerabilities.description: The reports search endpoint's `query` parameter is concatenated directly into a raw SQL LIKE clause in the reports service layer instead of being passed as a bound parameter.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to alter the query's logic (e.g. bypass the search filter entirely, or with a different payload extract data beyond what the search feature is meant to expose).

vulnerabilities.description: The document download endpoint accepts a multi-segment `name` path parameter and passes it to `resolve_document_path()` in the documents service layer, which joins it directly onto the documents directory with no containment check, allowing `../` sequences to escape the intended directory.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to read arbitrary files on the server outside the documents folder.

vulnerabilities.description: The integration DNS-check endpoint embeds the `hostname` parameter directly into a double-quoted shell command string and executes it with shell=True, without escaping or validating the value.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to break out of the intended command via shell metacharacters and execute arbitrary OS commands with the privileges of the server process.

vulnerabilities.description: The integration preview endpoint passes the `url` parameter directly to a server-side HTTP client with no allowlist or validation of the target host.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to make the server issue arbitrary outbound HTTP requests, including to internal-only services not otherwise reachable from outside the network.

vulnerabilities.description: The report draft resume endpoint base64-decodes and unpickles the `state` parameter with no integrity check or restriction on the unpickled type.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to submit a crafted pickle payload that executes arbitrary code on the server the moment it is deserialized.
vulnerabilities.poc: see POC.md "Insecure deserialization" section (crafted pickle payload via os.system)

vulnerabilities.description: The report-open endpoint redirects the user to the `return_to` query parameter with no validation that the target is a relative path or an allowlisted host.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to craft a link that appears to originate from this application but redirects the victim to an attacker-controlled site (e.g. for phishing).

vulnerabilities.description: The report filter endpoint evaluates the `expression` parameter directly with Python's eval(), passing only a local-variable dict that does not restrict access to builtins.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to execute arbitrary Python code, and via __import__, arbitrary OS commands, on the server.
